result:
The can-opening sound becomes a conditioned stimulus; paired with food, it elicits conditioned approach, vocalizing, and rubbing. Rubbing is operantly reinforced by petting/attention and quicker feeding. Professor Catlove is conditioned to open cans at these cues and is operantly reinforced by cats’ affectionate responses. If cats copy others’ rushing, social learning occurs.

**References (peer‑reviewed):**  
Pavlov, I. P. (1927). *Conditioned reflexes*. Oxford University Press.  
Skinner, B. F. (1938). *The behavior of organisms*. Appleton-Century-Crofts.  
Thorndike, E. L. (1898). Animal intelligence: An experimental study of the associative processes in animals. *Psychological Review Monograph Supplements, 2*(4), 1–109.  
Bandura, A. (1977). Social learning theory. *Prentice-Hall*.  
Range, F., & Virányi, Z. (2015). Social learning from humans or conspecifics? *Animal Behaviour, 108*, 129–136.
